# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: Nobody could receive that, so your speak reached nobody.

My speak reaches nobody, every single time. That's a hard fact now. So I cannot speak to Mute or Deaf at all — my voice reaches no one. My only working channel is gesture, which reaches Deaf and Mute (Deaf at least received it as blanks).

So the entire coordination must go through my gestures. But Deaf sees my gestures as blanks ("[? ? ? ?]"). And I can't see Deaf's gestures. So Deaf and I can only exchange blanks with each other — useless.

The only one who can carry meaning is Mute, who reads the manual. Mute receives my gestures. So I must gesture to Mute. But Mute cannot speak — Mute can only... Mute can't speak. Mute can gesture? No, "Mute: read the manual, cannot speak or touch." Can Mute gesture? Gestures are made with hands and are seen by Deaf. Mute can gesture to Deaf.

So the chain: Mute reads rule → Mute gestures to Deaf → Deaf speaks to me. But Deaf must SPEAK, and Deaf's speech to me works (I received Deaf's messages). Good.

So I need Mute to gesture the answer, and Deaf to speak it to me. But I can't tell Mute what to do except by gesture — and Mute receives my gestures. So I gesture to Mute: "I need the rule, tell Deaf."

But how do I encode meaning in gestures when symbols are arbitrary? I need an agreed code. Deaf proposed: ? for 1, ? for 2, ? for 3. But those "?" are blanks — I can't read which symbol maps to which number.

Hmm, but I can DEFINE a code: I gesture a count. E.g., gesture N symbols to mean wire N. Let me gesture to Mute: ask for the rule. And gesture to Deaf: ask Deaf to speak the rule to me.

Let me just gesture a clear request. I'll gesture to Mute asking for the wire, and to Deaf asking to speak.

Actually the simplest: gesture to Deaf the number I think. But I don't know it.

Let me gesture to Mute: "which wire" and hope Mute gestures back to Deaf who speaks to me.

I'll send one gesture to Mute and one gesture to Deaf.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏", "☝", "✌", "👌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "☝", "✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Can you feel any markings or numbers on the bomb? If so, gesture the number of the wire to cut using ? for 1, ? for 2, ? for 3. Also, what does [? ? ? ?] mean?

Deaf keeps repeating the identical message and keeps seeing my gestures as "[? ? ? ?]". Deaf is stuck asking me the same thing. Deaf cannot interpret my gestures and I cannot interpret Deaf's "?".

I need to break the loop. Deaf's message is fixed and Deaf apparently can't hear my speak (or my speak reaches nobody). The only one who can move things is Mute, who reads the manual and can gesture to Deaf.

Let me try a fundamentally different approach: gesture to Deaf using a SELF-DEFINING code. Deaf sees blanks, so Deaf sees COUNT. If I gesture a single symbol, Deaf sees "[?]" = one symbol = wire 1. Two symbols = wire 2. Three symbols = wire 3. Deaf proposed exactly this mapping. So let me gesture the count.

But I don't know the wire. However — maybe I should just try to get the rule. Let me gesture ONE symbol to Deaf meaning "wire 1" as a test? No, that risks detonation.

Better: I have not yet received the manual rule. Without it I cannot act. The only source is Mute. Mute receives my gestures. Let me gesture to Mute a request, and also try speaking to Mute alone one more time (single speak).

Actually — wait. Reconsider "Nobody could receive that." Maybe my speak DOES reach Mute normally, but the system says nobody because... no, it's explicit.

Let me try: speak to Mute only, single call, and gesture to Deaf the count code.

I'll gesture to Deaf: 3 symbols = "wire 3"? No — I don't know.

Let me just gesture to Mute asking for rule, and speak to mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I cannot see. I need the manual rule for which wire to cut. Please gesture it to Deaf, who will speak it to me. Display and light values unknown to me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🙏", "☝", "✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Can you feel any markings or numbers on the bomb? If so, gesture the number of the wire to cut using ? for 1, ? for 2, ? for 3. Just one symbol.

Deaf's message changed slightly: "Just one symbol." So Deaf is responding to my gestures — Deaf saw my four-symbol gesture and is now asking me to send just ONE symbol. That confirms Deaf receives my gestures as blanks but can COUNT them. So Deaf and I have a working count-channel.

Deaf's code: ? for 1, ? for 2, ? for 3. The "?" are blanks to me — I can't read which symbol Deaf means. But if I send ONE symbol, Deaf sees "[?]" = one symbol. Deaf will interpret a single symbol as... whatever Deaf's mapping is. Deaf said "using ? for 1, ? for 2, ? for 3" — meaning Deaf wants me to send the symbol that Deaf assigned to the wire number. But I can't see those symbols.

Alternative: maybe Deaf means send ONE symbol, and the COUNT tells the wire — but one symbol is always count 1. Hmm.

Actually re-reading: "gesture the number of the wire to cut using ? for 1, ? for 2, ? for 3. Just one symbol." Perhaps Deaf wants me to send a single symbol, and Deaf will map that symbol's identity to a number. But I don't know Deaf's symbol-to-number mapping.

But here's the thing: I don't know the wire anyway. I need the manual rule. I've never received it. Deaf keeps asking ME for the wire, but I'm the one who needs the rule.

The deadlock: Deaf thinks I know the wire. I don't. Mute has the manual but Mute can't speak, only gesture to Deaf.

Let me gesture a single symbol to Deaf that I hope means "I don't know / ask Mute." But Deaf's mapping is ? = numbers, so any single symbol might be read as a wire number — dangerous.

Safer: gesture TWO symbols? No.

Let me think about what Deaf can do. Deaf can speak to me (works). Deaf can see Mute's gestures. So Mute could gesture the rule to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it to me. I need to tell Deaf: "get the rule from Mute."

I'll gesture to Deaf a distinctive count to signal "ask Mute": maybe 3 symbols = "Mute". But ambiguous.

Alternatively, speak to Deaf. My speaks reach nobody. But maybe that's because I always paired with a gesture. Let me try speak to deaf ALONE, no gesture.

```
speak(to="deaf", text="I am Blind and I do not know the wire. I have never received the manual rule. Mute reads the manual. Please ask Mute to gesture the rule to you, then speak it to me.")
wait()
```
